earlier_receipt: Fresh PyPI download of all 11 asdk_plugin_*==2.0.0b3 wheels (fc/dl/b030r/un/), 54 swagger.json files, of which 48 match agraph.d.s.g.v1.API. Example of a match, .../abor_lot/v1/AborLotAPI/swagger.json:18: "x-aladdin-spec-id": "agraph.accounting.transactions.abor_lot.v1.AborLotAPI". claim: Aladdin Compute: A hosted space where developers run Python next to their Aladdin data
earlier_receipt: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/blackrock/aladdinsdk/main/README.md L179: "AladdinSDK can run on a developer's local machine or in Aladdin Studio Compute sessions."; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/blackrock/aladdinsdk/main/aladdinsdk/common/secrets/fsutil.py L29-30: "local development environment or in Aladdin Compute sessions to read secret files injected by Vault init container."; .../aladdinsdk/config/utils/user_settings_file_util.py L33: `_ENV_VAR_NOTEBOOK_USER_NAME = "NB_USER"  # For Aladdin Compute run modes`; aladdinsdk 2.0.0b10 (PyPI) common/authentication/oauth/local_token_server_client.py: "Client for communicating with the gateway's local token server running in aladdin-compute run mode." Negative: on https://www.blackrock.com/aladdin/platforms/products/apis the 'Aladdin Compute' link goes to /aladdin/platforms/products/aladdin-studio; /aladdin/products/aladdin-compute and /aladdin/platforms/products/aladdin-compute both return HTTP 404. No new web searches were run because the turn's search budget was used up, and Wayback was not used.
earlier_finding: The first checker was too harsh on 'hosted'. The SDK source (source 23 repo) shows Compute sessions are platform-run containers: secrets are 'injected by Vault init container', there is a notebook user (NB_USER), and a gateway with a token server. So 'hosted' and 'run Python' are supported. Only 'next to their Aladdin data' has no public quote; it is an inference from the injected API, ADC and S3 credentials. The row also cites no source. Fix: cite 23 and reword to 'a hosted environment (Compute sessions) where developers run Python against Aladdin's APIs and Data Cloud', or drop 'next to their Aladdin data'.

claim: the catalog, guides, notebooks and samples sit behind a client login
earlier_receipt: (1) Source 24, https://www.blackrock.com/aladdin/platforms/products/apis: "Aladdin Studio documentation teaches you how Aladdin API requests are built, authorized, and processed in our system. Get a head start building with developer guides Download Python Jupyter Notebooks, or cut and paste code samples ... Our Data Dictionary allows you to explore Aladdin data". The page has no link to these resources, only "Sign In" (Okta login.epl link) and "Contact us to learn more", and it never mentions a login requirement. (2) curl https://www.blackrock.com/apps/aladdin-developer-portal/ returns "302 https://aladdin-login.blackrock.com/oauth2/v1/authorize?client_id=0oangjmoyueyPY1VC357&response_type=code&scope=openid%20email%20profile...". (3) Fresh PyPI asdk_plugin_platform 2.0.0b3, scratchpad/fc/dl/b033r/pkg/asdk_plugin_platform/agraph/platform/identity/user/v1/UserAPI/swagger.json:13: "[Developer Guide]: apps/aladdin-developer-portal/#/guides/developer-guide" and "An Aladdin User is a person or a system account that can login into\n Aladdin client's website". (4) The Aladdin Studio page (blackrock.com/aladdin/products/aladdin-studio) says only "Start building in minutes with developer guides, code snippets, and convenient documentation", with no mention of a login.
earlier_finding: The claim is true in substance, but source 24 does not say it, so the citation is incomplete. Add source 6 (the UserAPI spec puts the Developer Guide at apps/aladdin-developer-portal), and/or state the observed fact that this URL redirects to the Aladdin Okta login (aladdin-login.blackrock.com). Only the guides are tied directly to the portal. That the catalog, notebooks and samples sit behind the same login is an inference from the lack of any public link, so softer wording would be safer, e.g. 'reached through the login-gated Aladdin developer portal'. My WebSearch budget was used up, so I verified with direct fetches and the fresh PyPI package.
